json_valid.problem: Parses. All 8 sections have title/plain/deeper/sources; glossary, failure_modes, aha_moments, timeline, what_this_supports, unverified present.

Parses; keys id, analogies, overcame_it, serendipity, cross_links, unverified. Note: devlog.json also exists in docs/data (not in scope). citation_checks.claim: Kraken 2 reduces memory use by about 85% versus Kraken 1 (Wood, Lu, Langmead, Genome Biology 2019)
citation_checks.note: Abstract: reducing memory usage by 85%; Genome Biology 2019, 20:257.

citation_checks.claim: Ye et al. 2019 Cell benchmarked 20 classifiers; most exceed 0.8 AUPR at species level; many report large numbers of low-abundance false positives
Pearson 1897 first described spurious correlation for data expressed as proportions (via Gloor et al. 2017)
citation_checks.note: Supported, but page says 'compositional data', not 'proportions'; Pearson 1897 reference title is 'a form of spurious correlation'. Wording slightly stronger than source.

citation_checks.claim: Canard and Sarfati (Pasteur Institute) patent reversible terminator chemistry, published 13 October 1994
citation_checks.note: Supported via patent CA 2158975 reference dated 1994-10-13; article text does not itself say 'patent'. Wikipedia is a weak source; cite the patent.

citation_checks.claim: Standard Kraken2 database has no fungi (archaea, bacteria, viral, human, UniVec_Core only)
citation_checks.note: Manual lists fungi as a separate optional library. Confidence default 0.0 and k=35, l=31 also confirmed.

citation_checks.claim: Sylph published in Nature Biotechnology (Shaw and Yu 2024), containment ANI with low-coverage correction
citation_checks.note: Confirmed. Page says accurate ANI down to 0.1x coverage. Timeline year should be checked against 2024 if it says otherwise.

citation_checks.claim: Gu, Miller, Chiu review, Annual Review of Pathology (author manuscript 2019)
citation_checks.note: Right paper, but journal version is 2018 (vol 14, Oct 2018); 2019 is only the PMC manuscript date. q_decisions.json title says 'Gu, Miller, Chiu 2019': fix to 2018 (or 'PMC 2019').

citation_checks.claim: Kraken (2014): 909x faster than Megablast, over 4.1 million reads per minute
citation_checks.note: INCONCLUSIVE: Springer redirected to an auth cookie page. Figures are widely cited from the abstract but were not confirmed here.

citation_checks.claim: Salter et al. 2014 show reagent/lab contamination affects sequencing results and recommend negative controls
citation_checks.note: INCONCLUSIVE: PubMed returned a cookie page. Claim is consistent with known BMC Biology 2014 paper but not confirmed in this pass.

citation_checks.claim: Bracken published in PeerJ Computer Science 2017 (Lu, Breitwieser, Thielen, Salzberg)
citation_checks.note: INCONCLUSIVE: HTTP 403. Site itself already flags this in unverified.

citation_checks.claim: ZymoBIOMICS D6300 by cell count: L. fermentum about 21.9%, B. subtilis 10.3%, S. cerevisiae 0.29%
citation_checks.note: INCONCLUSIVE: PDF text not extractable by fetch tool or by simple stream decompression. Central to the site's best 'aha' (12% is DNA, not cells), so it needs a manual check against the Zymo product page. Also the URL is a reseller copy, not Zymo.

missing_topics: A one-paragraph 'bottom line' for a founder: what would we conclude if the benchmark shows X vs Y, and what decision does it change (buy, build, trust a vendor, pick a tool).
Cost and runtime of our own benchmark in plain terms (CPU hours, RAM needed for 8 GB vs 16 GB database, why 8 vs 16 GB was chosen, laptop vs server).
What 'first N read pairs' means in plain words and how large N is, with a visual of how many reads each organism gets at that N.
A worked example of reading one result row end to end (true 12%, tool says 14%, is that good) with precision/recall explained on this concrete mock.
Reproducibility: exact tool versions, command lines, parameters (confidence value used, Bracken read length and threshold), seeds, and how to rerun; links to the code repository.
Why results on a mock will differ from real samples (stool, soil, clinical) and what a follow-up real-sample validation would need.
Licensing and commercial-use status of each tool and database (Kraken2 MIT, Bracken, MetaPhlAn licence, Zymo/ENA data terms) for a founder considering a product.

Who the competing tools and commercial services are (Kaiju, Centrifuge, Sylph, CZ ID, One Codex, etc.) and why only these four are tested; Sylph and Centrifuge are described but not benchmarked, which is easy to misread.
Data privacy/regulatory note: why public mock data avoids human-data issues, and what changes with patient samples (HIPAA/GDPR, human read removal).
Glossary index or search that spans all six topic files, and a short 'start here' reading order.

Limitations of the benchmark itself in one place: two mocks, one lab, one sequencing run each, nominal truth uncertain, MetaPhlAn index version newer than Kraken databases (dated 2025-04 vs 2026), so databases are not equal vintage.
Negative-control interpretation: what counts as a false positive in a single-isolate run versus real contamination or strain-level near neighbours.
Unclassified reads: what fraction is expected and why 'classified %' is not accuracy.

Strain/species naming mapping table (Lactobacillus fermentum to Limosilactobacillus fermentum, etc.) showing exactly how the truth table was harmonised across NCBI and MetaPhlAn naming, since this is an unverified item that directly changes scores.
A summary of unverified items for the whole site in one place with plan to close them, rather than seven per-page lists.

overstated.text: Mock composition and run accessions stated as fact: 'D6300 even mock (MiSeq 2x151, ERR2984773); D6310 log mock (HiSeq 2x101, ERR2935805) ... Nicholls et al. 2019 (ENA PRJEB29504)'
overstated.fix: q_ground_truth.json and q_evaluation.json list the ERR-to-mock mapping and PRJEB29504 as unverified, and q_algorithms says they come from the project brief. Add a visible 'taken from project setup, not independently confirmed' note wherever this sentence appears (q_algorithms, q_decisions, q_ground_truth), or verify at ENA and drop the caveat.

overstated.text: 'by cell count L. fermentum is about 22% and P. aeruginosa about 6%' and 'yeasts under 0.3% of cells' in aha_moments, plus king.json cross_link repeating it
overstated.fix: Source PDF could not be machine-read in this check and is a reseller copy. Cite the Zymo manual table directly, and note that strain/lot changes after ZRC190633 may shift values; or move to unverified until checked.

overstated.text: 'The two yeasts are 2% of the DNA but under 0.3% of the cells, because yeast genomes are big and diploid.'
overstated.fix: The 'because' explanation is the author's inference (genome size and ploidy), not sourced. Say 'largely because yeast genomes are much larger than bacterial genomes'; drop 'diploid' unless sourced.
Journal publication is Annual Review of Pathology 2018 (vol 14, Oct 2018); 2019 is only the PMC manuscript date.

overstated.text: Timeline: 'Karl Pearson first described the spurious-correlation problem for data expressed as proportions'
overstated.fix: Say 'for compositional data (as Gloor et al. 2017 credit to Pearson 1897)'.

overstated.text: Timeline: 'Canard and Sarfati ... patent reversible terminator chemistry ... foundation of sequencing by synthesis'
overstated.fix: Cite the patent (CA 2158975) rather than Wikipedia, and soften 'the foundation of' to 'an early basis for Illumina-style sequencing by synthesis'.

overstated.text: 'Kraken ... thousands of times faster than BLAST-style search (the 2014 paper reports 909 times faster than Megablast)'
overstated.fix: 'Thousands of times' contradicts the 909x figure quoted in the same sentence. Change to 'hundreds of times faster than Megablast (909x in the 2014 paper)', and confirm from the paper abstract.

overstated.text: Statements that Kraken2 default confidence 0 'reports many species not in the sample' and that classified reads approach zero above confidence 0.4
overstated.fix: The 0.4 figure is already flagged as from a search summary; mark the aha/failure_mode that relies on it as 'reported by one study, unchecked' in the visible text, not only in the unverified list.

overstated.text: '16S usually stops at genus level and ignores viruses, fungi'; 'shotgun costs 2-3 times more' ; 'shallow shotgun approaches 16S cost'
overstated.fix: Cost and resolution figures come from vendor blogs and snippets (per own unverified list). Attach 'vendor-reported, varies widely' next to the figure in the body text. Note that 16S primers can target fungi (ITS) so 'ignores fungi' should read 'standard bacterial 16S ignores fungi'.

overstated.text: 'Reads are roughly proportional to DNA mass' (used to justify scoring yeast against 2%)
overstated.fix: Flagged unverified, but it is the basis of the scoring logic. State it as an assumption that the benchmark tests, not a property: observed read share can differ because of extraction and GC bias.

overstated.text: 'Database choice often matters more than algorithm' and 'the 8 GB and 16 GB indexes drop information / lose sensitivity'
overstated.fix: Own unverified list admits no source quantifies the first and the specific losses are unknown. Reword to 'can matter as much as the algorithm' and 'down-sampling can drop some genomes (which ones is not checked here)'.

overstated.text: Statements about the LEMMI and CAMI results and Portik et al. 2022 findings
overstated.fix: Built from search summaries only. Prefix each with 'per the abstract' or remove numbers; do not present rankings as established.

overstated.text: Analogies and 'overcame_it' stories (CASP, art forgery, wine judging, STARD) presented as sourced stories
